title: Iceberg REST commit failure and restart recovery
description: Exercise exact commit retry before upstream admission, reconciliation after an accepted response is lost, and durable recovery when a catalog restarts while a request body is in flight, with config-gated idempotency content binding.

capabilities.description: Observe committed state through a direct catalog endpoint.
Commit a standard set-properties update with current requirements.
Retry the exact request after a disconnected response.
When config advertises idempotency-key-lifetime, bind a key to exact request content.

steps.description: Create a run-owned namespace and table through standard Iceberg REST.
Disconnect one commit before forwarding it.
Prove the property is absent, retry the exact request, and prove it is present.
Forward one commit, observe upstream success, and disconnect its response.
Prove accepted state directly and retry exactly, accepting equivalent success or safe CAS conflict.
When advertised, send different content with the same UUIDv7 key and prove it cannot mutate state.
Transmit the first commit-body byte to the catalog and hold the rest at a deterministic proxy gate.
Restart only the catalog service while the standard Iceberg REST request remains in flight, then release the held connection.
Prove the partial request did not mutate durable state, retry the exact request, and prove accepted state after recovery.
Drop the table and namespace and remove the fresh Docker project and volumes.

assertions.description: The first before-upstream commit returns no HTTP response.
Direct load proves the property is absent before retry.
The exact retry succeeds and the property becomes accepted.
The client receives no response although the proxy observed upstream success.
Direct load proves the property was accepted before retry.
Exact retry is equivalent success or a safe conflict, with accepted state unchanged.
When advertised, same-key different-content cannot mutate state and should return conflict rather than cached success.
The proxy records exactly one sanitized during-upstream event before catalog restart.
Direct load after restart proves the partial request did not set the property.
The exact retry succeeds and durable state contains the accepted property.
The table, namespace, project containers, and project volumes are removed.
